title: A History of Christmas in America

source.name: VOA Learning English — A History of Christmas in America
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: During this period, there was no set way of celebrating the day, which was not yet an official holiday. Communities around the country honored the day in different ways. Some observed Christmas as an important Christian religious day honoring the birth of Jesus. Others celebrated the day with parties, music, drinking and eating. And, some communities did not celebrate the day at all.
But, it was during this period that Americans began to reinvent the holiday. They combined ancient Christmas traditions from different cultures with modern American influences.
In 1819, the popular American writer Washington Irving wrote a series of five essays published in a book called The Sketchbook of Geoffrey Crayon, Gent .

The essays describe a wealthy British landowner who invites his farm workers into his home to celebrate Christmas. The landowner recreates a traditional Christmas as it would have been celebrated in the distant past. Irving praised this looking back to ancient traditions. He liked the idea of different levels of society coming together to enjoy a festive and peaceful holiday. Washington Irving seemed to express concern about the lack of such unifying Christmas traditions in modern America.

Penne Restad wrote a book Christmas in America: A History . It shows how Americans began to slowly shape Christmas into a unifying national holiday during the first half of the 19th century. She describes how Christmas had different meanings for Americans who came from different cultural and religious backgrounds. Many immigrants brought Christmas traditions from their own countries.

Religion played a big role in how an American might celebrate the holiday. Calvinist Christians banned the celebration of Christmas. But groups such as Episcopalians and Moravians honored the day with religious services and seasonal decorations .

Christmas became an important time for families to celebrate at home. More and more Christian Americans also began to follow the European traditions of Christmas trees and giving gifts. Christians believed that the tree represented Jesus and was also a sign of new beginnings. German immigrants brought their tradition of putting lights, sweets and toys on the branches of evergreen trees placed in their homes.

This tradition of setting up a Christmas tree soon spread to many American homes. So did the practice of giving people presents. As these traditions increased in popularity, the modern trade and business linked to Christmas also grew.

As Christmas became more popular, some states declared the day a state holiday. Louisiana was the first state to make the move in 1837. By 1860, 14 other states had followed. It was not until 1870 that President Ulysses Grant made Christmas a federal holiday.

Americans already knew old Christmas songs that came from England and other areas of Europe. But many new American Christmas songs started to become popular. For example, in eighteen forty-nine, a religious leader from Massachusetts wrote the words to It Came Upon a Midnight Clear .The song J ingle Bells appeared seven years later. And, a year later, a religious leader in Williamsport, Pennsylvania wrote the song We Three Kings of Orient Are .

This character is based on the story of Saint Nicholas, a Christian holy person believed to have lived in the third century. Saint Nicholas became known as a protector of children. Different cultures have given him different names. These include Sinterklaas, Kris Kringle and Father Christmas. But for most Americans his most popular name would become Santa Claus.

In the 19th century, many Dutch immigrants living in the United States celebrated the feast of Saint Nicholas on December 6. Saint Nicholas was especially important to New Yorkers because of their history as a Dutch colony. In 1809, Washington Irving published his History of New York . It lists Saint Nicholas as the patron saint of New Yorkers. He describes the saint wearing a low hat, large pants, and smoking a pipe. Does this description sound familiar?

questions.q: What can be concluded about Christmas in America in the early nineteenth century?
options: It was already a national holiday that every state observed in the same way
There was no single way of keeping it, and some places ignored it completely
It was forbidden by law in most places, so people celebrated it in secret
Almost every community kept it quietly as a purely religious day of prayer
questions.explain: Đoạn 1–2: “no set way of celebrating”, “not yet an official holiday”; có nơi cầu nguyện, có nơi tiệc tùng, có nơi không ăn mừng. Chỉ phái Calvin cấm (đoạn 6), nên “forbidden in most places” sai.

questions.q: What was Washington Irving’s attitude to the Christmas described in his 1819 essays?
options: He feared it was becoming far too religious for modern readers
He criticised it as an old custom that people ought to forget
He admired it because it brought rich and poor together
He thought it was too expensive for ordinary families to copy at home
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: Irving “praised” việc nhìn lại truyền thống cổ và “liked the idea of different levels of society coming together” → ông ngưỡng mộ vì nó gắn kết các tầng lớp.

questions.q: According to Penne Restad, why did Christmas mean different things to different Americans?
options: Most families refused to follow any customs that came from Europe
The government kept changing the date of the holiday from year to year
The population included people from many different cultures and faiths
Shops advertised the holiday in a different way in each region
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: Giáng sinh có ý nghĩa khác nhau với người Mỹ “who came from different cultural and religious backgrounds”; nhiều dân nhập cư mang theo tập quán riêng.

questions.q: How did the Episcopalians and Moravians differ from the Calvinists over Christmas?
options: They marked the day with church services and decorations, which the Calvinists would not allow
They gave up celebrating the day, while the Calvinists decorated their homes with candles
They held parties with music and drinking, while the Calvinists attended church
They gave presents to children, while the Calvinists preferred to travel abroad
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: Calvinists “banned the celebration”; Episcopalians và Moravians “honored the day with religious services and seasonal decorations”.

questions.q: What was one result of the spread of Christmas trees and gift-giving in American homes?
options: Families stopped celebrating Christmas at home and met in public places
State governments ended their official recognition of the holiday
Shops and companies connected with the holiday did more business
Immigrants gave up the customs they had brought from their own countries
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: khi các truyền thống này phổ biến “the modern trade and business linked to Christmas also grew”.

questions.q: Which statement about Christmas becoming an official holiday is supported by the text?
options: The federal government declared it before any state had done so
Louisiana made it a holiday in the same year as the federal government
Fifteen states had recognised the day before the federal government did
Louisiana was the only state to recognise it before the year 1870
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: Louisiana năm 1837 + “14 other states” đến 1860 = 15 bang; liên bang chỉ công nhận năm 1870 (Tổng thống Grant).

questions.q: Washington Irving had mentioned Saint Nicholas in a book that appeared ten years before his Christmas essays.
questions.explain: Đoạn 12: “History of New York” (1809) nhắc đến Saint Nicholas; đoạn 3: các bài tiểu luận về Giáng sinh xuất bản năm 1819 → cách nhau mười năm.

questions.q: The words of “Jingle Bells” were written by a religious leader.
questions.explain: Đoạn 10 nói hai bài hát khác do các nhà lãnh đạo tôn giáo viết lời, còn “Jingle Bells” chỉ được nói là “appeared seven years later”, không nêu tác giả.

str.explain: More and more + danh từ: sự gia tăng liên tục.

str.ex: The landowner recreates a traditional Christmas as it would have been celebrated in the distant past.
str.explain: would have + V3 trong mệnh đề as: cách tổ chức “có lẽ đã” diễn ra thế nào.
